questions.prompt: A child context made with extend({ label: 'loop' }) calls child.get('llm'). Where does the adapter come from?
options: A copy of the store that extend made for the child
The root's store, found through the child's prototype
A new store that the child creates on first read
Nowhere: a child can only read its own properties
questions.explanation: The child has no store of its own, so JavaScript looks in its prototype, the root, and finds the one shared store there.

questions.prompt: After child = root.extend({ label: 'loop' }), what is root.label?
options: 'loop', because the child shares its properties with the root
An error, because the root has no prototype
undefined, because own properties of a child never reach the parent
questions.explanation: extend puts label on the new child object only. The parent is not changed, so reading label on the root finds nothing.

questions.prompt: Why does the loop gain from calling ctx.get('llm') instead of importing llm.ts?
options: The code that builds the context can put a different adapter under the same name
The request to DeepSeek becomes faster
The model no longer needs the message history
The loop no longer needs a tool list
questions.explanation: The loop names the ability, not the file. A test or a second provider can provide its own llm service and the loop does not change.
